properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: js-sha256 (direct dependency, packages/frontend/package.json:38) used in accountIdToHash() to pseudonymize account IDs before sending to RudderStack analytics — privacy hygiene for telemetry, not a security control (NEAR account IDs are public identifiers). SHA-256 is not meaningfully quantum-vulnerable (Grover square-root only). Companion site found by this scout: account-with-lockup.js:165 uses the same library for lockup-account-ID derivation — reported as a separate finding.

components.name: Node.js tls sessions on default settings (Node.js version unknown)

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Ops CLI command disable-2fa opens HTTPS sessions via global fetch() (Node.js default TLS settings): lines 61 and 68 download NEAR contract WASM from github.com; the command also talks to NEAR RPC/helper endpoints via near-api-js. Node version is not pinned anywhere in this tree, so post-quantum capability is undecidable — Node offers X25519MLKEM768 by default only from 24.5.0. Independently confirmed by tls_sessions (2 call sites, same file). Changeable here: pin the Node version ≥24.5 or config
